lock.title: Lock this day for good?
lock.consequence: Afterwards this day can never be changed or deleted again, not by you and not by the operator. Its text, title, tags, values, cover, notes and photos stay exactly as they are now. You can still share it. Only deleting the whole account takes it away.
lock.readOnly: This day is locked. It cannot be changed any more.
lock.saveFirst: Save your changes first, then the day can be locked.

catchUp.title_one: {{count}} day with notes and no page
catchUp.title_other: {{count}} days with notes and no page
catchUp.text: You can still turn these notes into a page.
catchUp.sectionNone: Every day with notes has a page.

night.title: Which day does this belong to?
night.text: It is after midnight. Which day do your notes of tonight belong to? Your answer holds until 4 am, on all your devices.

series.shieldDays: Protects your streak on a missed day
series.shieldWeeks: Protects your streak in a week you miss

today.capture: What is on your mind? Just jot it down.
today.tagSuggestions: family, work, outdoors, autumn, health, friends, holiday, cooking, sport, thoughts
today.unreadable: Not readable. This note is damaged in the database and can only be deleted.
today.promptLabel: Your answer to the question of the day

quick.writeUpHint: At leisure, with values and photos
quick.writeUpHintAi: At leisure, with values, photos and the AI if you like

journal.title: Your journal
journal.nothing: Nothing found. Maybe it was written differently?
journal.empty: No day written down yet. In the evening your notes become the first page.

stats.title: Statistics
stats.intro: Made only from your own days. Nobody else sees this page.
stats.empty: No page written yet. Once you have written up your first day, your streak, your half year and more show up here.
stats.unreadable_one: {{count}} day could not be read and is missing here.
stats.unreadable_other: {{count}} days could not be read and are missing here.
stats.noValue: nexdiary is not asking for any value right now. You can switch values on under My account, Writing.
stats.needValue: That takes a few days with {{name}}.

tiles.shieldDays: Protects your streak on a missed day
tiles.shieldWeeks: Protects your streak in a week you miss
tiles.rescuedWeek: Streak saved in the week of {{date}}

calendar.title: Your half year
calendar.textValue: One square per day. The darker, the higher {{name}} is.
calendar.textWritten: One square per day you wrote.
calendar.label: Calendar of the last {{count}} weeks

series.title: {{name}} over time
series.text: Dots are single days, the line is the average over seven days. On average {{mean}} out of 10.
series.textNone: Dots are single days, the line is the average over seven days. There is no value in this period yet.
series.label: {{name}} over the last {{count}} days

weekdays.title: Your weekdays
weekdays.thin: To compare, it takes three days with a value on at least two weekdays.

together.title: What goes together
together.text: {{name}} on days like these, compared with the other days.
together.sentence: {{a}}: {{aMean}} on average over {{aDays}} days. {{b}}: {{bMean}} on average over {{bDays}} days.
together.note: Together does not mean because. It only shows what often happens together for you.
together.thin: That takes more days: at least {{min}} on each side of a comparison.

extremes.title: My best and my worst day
extremes.text: By {{name}}. With a tie the more recent day counts.

shared.title: Shared
shared.intro: Single days you show each other in the family. Everything else stays with each of you.
shared.noneByMe: You have not shared a day yet. Open a day and tap “Share”.
shared.noneWithMe: Nobody has shared a day with you yet.
shared.note: Only ever a single day is shared, with particular people. It cannot be passed on, and whoever shared it can take it back at any time.
shared.gone: This day is not (or no longer) shared with you.
shared.heartHint: A quiet sign that you have read it. Nothing more.

capsules.title: Time capsules
capsules.intro: Letters that open only on a certain day. To yourself in a year, or to Mia on her 18th birthday.
capsules.noneWaiting: No time capsule is waiting for you right now.
capsules.noneSent: You have not sent a time capsule yet.
capsules.sealedHint: Letters to yourself stay closed until the day
capsules.withdrawn: Taken back. Nobody can see it any more.
capsules.withdrawText: It disappears for everybody it is for and cannot be brought back.
capsules.gone: This time capsule is no longer there.
capsules.todayByGone: An account deleted since wrote this letter {{ago}}, on {{date}}.
capsules.pickFuture: Please choose a date in the future.
capsules.titlePlaceholder: Heading, say: To me, in a year
capsules.textPlaceholderSelf: What is on your mind right now? What do you hope for when you read this?
capsules.textPlaceholderOthers: What would you like to tell {{names}} when the day has come?
capsules.photosPause: A short pause, it goes on in a moment.
capsules.hintSelf: A letter to yourself is sealed: until the day you can neither read nor change it, only take it back.
capsules.hintOthers_one: Until then {{names}} only sees that a letter from you is waiting, not what it says. You can change it or take it back until the day.
capsules.hintOthers_other: Until then {{names}} only see that a letter from you is waiting, not what it says. You can change it or take it back until the day.
capsules.hintPush: On the day itself a message comes to the phone.

family.title: Family question
family.text: One question a day for the whole family, for every age.
family.join: Take part in the family question
family.hint: Every day one question for everybody who takes part. You see the others' answers as soon as you have answered yourself.
family.leave: If you stop taking part, nobody sees your answers any more. What of them is in your notes stays.

language.title: Language
language.text: Applies to your account. The others in the family choose their own.

looks.title: Themes
looks.text: For your account only, on every device. Every theme comes light and dark; on the left you see the day, on the right the evening.

salbei.name: Sage
salbei.mood: Garden, tea, a deep breath. The calmest.

terrakotta.name: Terracotta
terrakotta.mood: Fired clay, a fire in the hearth. The warmest of all.

pflaume.name: Plum
pflaume.mood: Autumnal, a little dreamy. Calm without being cold.

altrosa.name: Dusty rose
altrosa.mood: Rosewood, letter paper. Soft and personal.

tinte.name: Ink
tinte.mood: Fountain-pen blue on paper. The classic diary, warm thanks to the paper.

values.title: My values
values.text: What you want to rate from 1 to 10 every day. Only you see them, unless you share them with a day.
values.ownPlaceholder: say sport, headaches, time with the kids
values.name: Name
values.deleteText: {{name}} will no longer be asked for. What you entered on earlier days stays with those days.
values.none: No values yet. Add one below.

goal.title: Writing goal
goal.text: How often do you want to write? Your streak, your shields and the reminder for a weekly goal in danger are measured by it.
goal.label: How often do you want to write?
goal.daily: {{count}} times a week, so every day
goal.hintDays: Your streak counts days in a row. A shield saves a missed day; you earn one for every 10 days in a row.
goal.hintWeeks: Your streak counts weeks in a row in which you reached your goal, whichever days you write on. A shield saves a week you miss; you earn one for every 4 weeks in a row that reached the goal.
goal.hintLong: A long entry of 300 words or more earns a shield as well, at most one a week.
goal.hintChange: Your streak is counted again with the new goal.

phone.title: On the phone
phone.text: For on the go: just one field, the keyboard already open, today's notes above it.
phone.quickStartHint: When you open nexdiary on your phone, you land right in the text field. "All" at the top leads to the whole app.
phone.also: Also: press and hold the nexdiary icon on the home screen and choose "Note", or share a text or a photo from another app to nexdiary.

layout.title: Layout of "Today"
layout.text: The screen you open every day.

page.name: Day page
page.idea: Everything on one page: write at the top, the day as a timeline below, then photos, values, wrapping up. The easiest to understand.

columns.name: Two columns
columns.idea: Writing and the notes on the left, the day on the right: wrapping up, values, photos, tags. Good on a computer, on the phone like the day page.

chat.name: Like a chat
chat.idea: Notes as messages to yourself, the text field at the bottom as in a messenger. Values and photos behind "Your day". The quickest on the phone.

journal.title: Journal layout
journal.text: How your days look when you page back.

blog.name: Blog
blog.idea: Large cards with a photo, the newest day big at the top. Browse it like a magazine.

timeline.name: Timeline
timeline.idea: Grouped by month, one line per day with a small picture. More at a glance, good for searching.

prompts.title: Writing prompts
prompts.text: Small questions for the days when nothing comes to mind. "Today" shows a question of the day; when you write in the evening you can add more.
prompts.showHint: Off: no question on "Today" and none while writing.
prompts.whichText: Switch whole groups on or off.

templates.title: Templates
templates.text: Fixed headings for your page. When the AI writes it up, it fills in only what your notes say about them, the rest stays empty.
templates.name: Name
templates.heading: Heading
templates.question: Question as a hint (may stay empty)
templates.defaultHint: It is preselected when you write, and the AI uses it in the morning. On any page you can pick another.
templates.examplesText: You get a copy that you can change freely afterwards.
templates.deleteText: "{{name}}" will be deleted. Pages you wrote with it stay as they are.

work.name: Work day
work.question4: What do I take with me?

immich.accountClosed: Your operator has not allowed Immich for your account.
immich.title: Immich
immich.text: Suggest the photos of your day straight from Immich. Everyone connects their own account; nexdiary only reads, and copies a photo only when you take it for a day.
immich.closed: Your operator has not allowed Immich.
immich.keyHint: In Immich under Account Settings → API Keys, with the permissions “asset.read”, “asset.view” and “asset.download”. Optionally “album.read” as well, so that you can browse albums too.
immich.suggest: Suggest the photos of the day
immich.suggestHint: “Today” shows the photos you took on that day.
immich.probed_one: Connection checked: Immich {{version}}, {{count}} photo of today.
immich.probed_other: Connection checked: Immich {{version}}, {{count}} photos of today.
immich.probedMore: Connection checked: Immich {{version}}, more than {{count}} photos of today.
immich.disconnected: Disconnected. The photos you took stay.

auth.name: Name
auth.nameHint: You sign in with it: 2 to 64 letters without accents, digits, dot, hyphen or underscore.

setup.title: Set up nexdiary
setup.text: The first account runs this server: it invites the family and may change every setting. It never sees the others' diaries.
setup.codeHint: It stands in the server log (docker logs nexdiary), or set NEXDIARY_SETUP_TOKEN.

login.title: Sign in
login.passwordOff: Sign-in with a password is turned off here. Only the operator can still use it.

code.title: Second factor
code.text: The code from your app, or a recovery code.
code.label: Code from the app
code.hint: Six digits. Or one of your recovery codes.
code.textPasskey: Sign in with your passkey, or give a recovery code.

invite.title: Invitation
invite.text: You are invited to nexdiary. Make yourself an account; your diary is seen only by those you show it to.
invite.invalidText: This invitation no longer works: it was used, has run out or was withdrawn. Ask for a new one.
invite.noWay: Sign-in with a password is off and no sign-in provider is set up. Ask the operator.
invite.haveAccount: This link is for a new account. You are signed in as {{name}} already and do not need it.

remember.label: Stay signed in on this device
remember.hint: Until you have not been here for 30 days. Good for your own phone, not for other people's devices.

setup2fa.title: Set up your second factor
setup2fa.text: The operator requires a second factor for every account that signs in with a password. Set it up to go on.
setup2fa.scan: Scan the code with an authenticator app, or type in the key. Then the code the app shows.
setup2fa.passkeyLater: Rather without an app? You can add a passkey afterwards under My account → Security.

codes.title: Your recovery codes
codes.text: Each one signs you in once, when the phone is not at hand. They are shown only now: keep them apart from the phone.

forgot.title: Forgot your password
forgot.text: Enter your name or your mail address. If there is an account with a mail address for it, we send a link with which you choose a new password.
forgot.label: Name or mail address
forgot.sent: If there is such an account, a link is on its way. It works once and for 24 hours.

reset.title: New password
reset.text: Choose a new password for {{name}}. Every device signs in again afterwards. Your second factor stays.
reset.invalidText: This link does not work any more: it was used or has run out. Ask for a new one, or tap "Forgot your password?" when signing in.
reset.doneText: You can sign in with the new password now.

about.subtitle: A diary for the family: gather during the day, write it down in the evening.
about.fontsText: nexdiary brings its fonts along, so that opening it asks no other server.

updates.title: Updates
updates.text: Whether a newer version of nexdiary is out.
updates.dailyHint: Asks GitHub for the newest release. Off: only when you press the button.
updates.whatGoesOut: Only the question goes out: a request to api.github.com for the newest release of nexdiary, with no names, entries or settings. It is the only call nexdiary makes on its own.

me.title: My account

profile.text: How the others in the family see you when you share a day with them.
profile.displayHintPassword: Empty shows your user name {{name}}; you still sign in with it.
profile.name: Name
profile.hint: A photo from your phone or camera. It is cut to a square, and nothing of the file but the picture is kept: no place, no device.

password.title: Password
password.done: Password changed. Every other device is signed out.

oidc.title: Sign-in provider
oidc.text: Sign in through {{name}}, besides the password.
oidc.linked: Linked: you can sign in through {{name}} and with your password.
oidc.linkedNow: Your account is linked to the provider.
oidc.how: Link your account with {{name}}, then both work. Your password confirms it is you; then it goes to {{name}} and back. There, its own second factor applies.

me.setupFirst: The operator requires a second factor. Set it up here, then you can go on.

ai.notAllowed: Your operator has not allowed the AI for your account.
ai.title: AI when writing
ai.text: Turns your notes of the day into a suggestion for the page. Only when you press "Write it up".
ai.mineHint: Off: the button "Write it up" disappears for you, and your texts never go to a model.

push.title: Notifications on your devices
push.text: Reminders come as a push straight to the phone or into the browser, even while nexdiary is closed. You sign up each device on its own.
push.name: Name of the device
push.ready: Not signed up yet. The browser will ask whether nexdiary may send notifications.
push.denied: The browser blocked notifications for nexdiary. Allow them in the settings of the site (the lock left of the address), then carry on here.
push.insecure: This address has no https, so push does not work. Open nexdiary at its https address.
push.iphone: On the iPhone it only works from the app on the home screen. Put nexdiary there and open it from there.
push.hintHttps: Push needs an address with https (or localhost).
push.hintIphone: On the iPhone it only works from the app on the home screen: Share, then “Add to Home Screen”. From iOS 16.4.
push.deniedNow: Notifications are not allowed. Without them nexdiary cannot send anything.
push.probeHint: Arrives on every device signed up.

remind.title: When to remind
remind.text: A gentle nudge when you have not written yet.
remind.days: After how many days without an entry
remind.skip: Do not remind me when I have written today
remind.skipHint: One note a day is enough.
remind.withPrompt: With a question of the day
remind.withPromptHint: The reminder brings a writing prompt along, such as “What made you happy today?”
remind.goalRisk: Remind me when my weekly goal is in danger
remind.goalRiskHint: At the chosen time, when you have not written today and the days left in the week only just suffice for your goal. For example: goal 3, 2 still open, Friday. It then replaces the other reminder of that day.
remind.goalText_one: {{count}} more entry for your weekly goal.
remind.goalText_other: {{count}} more entries for your weekly goal.
remind.previewGoal: When the weekly goal is in danger
remind.pauseText_one: Nothing written since yesterday. Fancy a few lines?
remind.pauseText_other: Nothing written for {{count}} days. Fancy a few lines?

devices.title: Signed-in devices
devices.text: Where you are signed in. A sign-in ends by itself after 30 days without use.
devices.notify: Tell me about a new sign-in
devices.notifyHint: By push to your devices and by mail: which device, which browser, roughly from where. If it was not you, one tap signs it off.
devices.endedAll: Every other device is signed out.

passkeys.title: Passkeys
passkeys.text: Sign in with your fingerprint, face or the device's PIN, without password and without code. A passkey counts as two factors by itself and cannot be phished.
passkeys.how: The browser will ask for your fingerprint, face or PIN. The passkey stays on the device or in your keychain.
passkeys.name: Name
passkeys.removeText: Nobody gets in with this passkey afterwards. Delete it on the device too when you no longer need it.
passkeys.unavailable: Passkeys work only over https (or localhost) and in browsers that know them.
passkeys.noAddressOperator: Enter the public address first (<settings>Settings → Sign-in</settings>).
passkeys.noAddressMember: Your operator has to enter the public address first.

twofactor.title: Second factor
twofactor.lead: Besides the password, a code from an app on your phone. Recovery codes on paper get you in when the phone is gone.
twofactor.provider: You sign in through the provider; its second factor applies.
twofactor.scan: Scan this code with the app, or type the key below into it. Then give the code the app shows, and your password.
twofactor.qr: QR code for the authenticator app
twofactor.passwordHint: Proves it is you at the keyboard.
twofactor.codesLead: Each code signs you in once, when the phone is not at hand. They are shown only now.
twofactor.renewText: The old recovery codes stop working. Give your password to make new ones.
twofactor.disableText: From then on the password alone signs you in. Give it to turn the second factor off.
twofactor.lowCodes: Few recovery codes left. Make new ones while you can still sign in.
twofactor.scanNoPassword: Scan this code with the app, or type the key below into it. Then give the code the app shows.
twofactor.required: It cannot be turned off: the operator requires it for everybody.

invite.noMail: Without a mail server nexdiary sends nothing: copy the link and pass it on yourself.
invite.once: The link works once. It is shown only now.

apiTokens.title: API tokens
apiTokens.text: For programs such as a card in nexdeck. A token reads what you may read, never more. A token changes nothing.
apiTokens.name: Name, so you know it again
apiTokens.shownOnce: Token “{{name}}” made. It is shown only now. Copy it into your program; nexdiary keeps only a checksum.
apiTokens.header: As a header in the program
apiTokens.off: The operator has not switched API tokens on. Ask them if you want to connect nexdiary with a program.
apiTokens.offOperator: Switch them on under Settings, API.
apiTokens.whatItDoesText: Every request carries the token in the header Authorization: Bearer, the answers are JSON. All the rest is in docs/api.md.

server.permissionsHint: Single accounts can be left out of the AI or Immich.
server.accountsHint: Who in your family uses nexdiary. As the operator you manage accounts, but you see no entries: every diary belongs to its own person only.
server.inviteText: Whoever follows the link makes an account of their own. Without a mail server you copy the link and pass it on yourself.
server.givePassword: Send a link for a password

promote.text: {{name}} may then change every setting of this server. An operator never sees the others' diaries either.

demote.text: {{name}} becomes a member and no longer reaches the server's settings.

delete.title: Delete {{name}}?
delete.text: The account is deleted with everything that belongs to it and cannot be brought back.

reset.title: Remove the second factor of {{name}}?
reset.text: For a lost phone: the code from the app, the passkeys and the recovery codes go, every device is signed out, and the person is told. At the next sign-in they set the second factor up again.

signout.title: Sign {{name}} out everywhere?
signout.text: Every device of the account has to sign in again.

block.title: Block {{name}}?
block.text: {{name}} no longer gets in, open sessions end at once. Unblocking works at any time.

unblock.title: Unblock {{name}}?
unblock.text: {{name}} can sign in again afterwards, with their own password or through the sign-in provider.

backup_restore.title: Restore this backup?
backup_restore.text: The current state is backed up first. nexdiary restarts, everybody signs in again.

backup_download.title: Download this backup?
backup_download.text: It holds every account and everything written. It is not encrypted.

backup_upload.title: Upload a backup?
backup_upload.text: The file joins the list of backups. Nothing is restored until you confirm it there.

two_factor_off.title: Stop requiring a second factor?
two_factor_off.text: Then a password alone is enough again to read a diary. Whoever has a second factor already keeps it.

provider_checks.title: Leave the second factor to the provider?
provider_checks.text: Whoever comes in through {{name}} is no longer asked for a second factor here. That is safe only when {{name}} requires one itself.

link.title: Send {{name}} a link to reset the password?
link.text: The person chooses their password themselves. The link goes by mail to their address when mail is set up, otherwise you get it once to pass on. The second factor stays.

server.passwordLoginHint: Off: members get in through the provider only. As the operator you can always use your password.
server.twoFactorRequiredHint: Every account must set it up before it gets any further: right after the password.
server.ownSecondFactorFirst: Set up your own second factor first (My account, Security), or you would be the first one who cannot go on.
server.publicUrlHint: The address nexdiary is reached under. Invitations and the provider use it.
server.secretKept: stored, leave empty to keep it
server.oidcAutoCreateHint: Off: only invited or linked accounts get in through the provider.

authentik.title: authentik in one step
authentik.text: With an API token that may create applications, nexdiary sets up provider and application in authentik by itself. The token is used for that only and not stored.

apiTokens.title: API tokens
apiTokens.text: Accounts connect nexdiary with programs such as nexdeck. A token only reads, and never more than its account. Off by default.
apiTokens.allowHint: Every account makes its own tokens under My account, Connections.
apiTokens.blockText: The token then answers like none, for good. The account sees it as “blocked by the operator” and can make a new one while API tokens are on.
apiTokens.offHint: When you switch API tokens off, every token answers 401. The tokens stay and work again when you switch them on.

server.mailHint: For invitations only. Without a server, the link to copy is enough.
server.backupsHint: One file with everything: accounts, settings and everything you write. A backup also holds the server's secrets; keep it like a password. Restoring shows a trial run first.
server.uploadedHint: Uploaded. It is in the list now: check it first, then restore.
server.checkOk: Complete: {{accounts}}, {{files}}. Restoring would add {{add}} and remove {{remove}}.
server.checkBad: Damaged: this backup cannot be restored.
server.checkOtherKey: This backup comes from another server. Its diaries are sealed with that server's master key, which is missing here. Put the old server's keys/master.key (or the file saved with “Save master key”, renamed to master.key) into the data folder and restart nexdiary first, then it works.
server.restarting: nexdiary restarts with the backup. The page reloads in a moment.
server.languagesHint: German and English are built in. Add more as a JSON file; missing texts fall back to English.
server.languageAdded: Language added. It appears under My account, Profile.
server.logHint: What the server did. Without the content of entries.
server.logClearText: Every line goes. New ones come as before.
server.checkNewer: This backup comes from a newer version of nexdiary. Update nexdiary first, then restore.
server.storageHint: How much each person may use for photos and drafts. 0 means no limit.

ai.title: AI to write the day up
ai.text: Applies to everyone in the family. The AI runs only when someone presses "Write it up", and everyone can switch it off for themselves in their account.
ai.noneNote: The button "Write it up" does not appear.
ai.localNote: Ollama or another service in the own network. Nothing leaves the house.
ai.messagesNote: Your own API key. When writing up, the notes go to the provider.
ai.openaiNote: Your own API key and address. When writing up, the notes go to the provider.
ai.keyKept: saved, leave empty to keep it
ai.probed: Saved. Test: the model answered in {{seconds}} seconds.
ai.outgoing: What goes out: when someone presses "Write it up", the notes of that one day with their times and, where a note answers a question, with the question. Without the name of the account, without the date, without photos and without ratings. Nothing else. Whoever does not want that switches the AI off in their account.
ai.keyLocalHint: Only when the service asks for one, such as LiteLLM. Ollama needs none.
ai.autoAllowedHint: Off: nobody can have the day before written up on its own in the morning. On: each person decides in their own account, where it is off from the start. The notes then go to the service set up here without a press of a button.

immich.title: Immich
immich.text: Everyone can connect their own Immich and take photos of the day from it. The address is a way into your network, so this works only on the hosts you allow here.
immich.allowedHint: Off from the start. Off, and nobody reaches an Immich through this server.
immich.hostsHint: One host per line, best with its port, such as immich.example.com:2283: then only that port holds. Without a port, every port of the host is allowed. Metadata addresses of cloud servers never.

push.title: Web Push
push.text: So that reminders reach the phone and the browser. Set up from the start; each person signs up their devices under My account → Reminders.
push.ready_one: Ready · {{count}} device signed up in the family
push.ready_other: Ready · {{count}} devices signed up in the family
push.contactHint: The services of Google, Apple and Mozilla ask for an address where they reach the operator. It stands in every message, nothing else of yours.
push.keysText: nexdiary made a key pair of its own at the first start. Making a new one signs every device off; each person has to sign them up again.
push.renewText: Every device in the family is signed off. Each person has to sign them up again under My account → Reminders.
push.renewed: New key pair made. Every device is signed off.
push.hostsHint: Messages go only to the services of Google, Mozilla, Apple and Microsoft. If a browser needs another one, enter its host here, one per line, such as push.example.com.
push.out: What goes out: an encrypted message to the push service of each browser (Google for Chrome, Apple for Safari, Mozilla for Firefox). Only the device can read it. It holds the reminder only, never an entry.

server.providerChecksHint: On: whoever comes in through {{name}} needs no second factor of their own here. Turn on only when {{name}} requires one itself.
server.withoutMasterKey: ⚠️ Without the master key a backup cannot be read, not even by you.

encryption.title: Encryption
encryption.text: Texts, notes, values and photos are sealed in the database, each person with a key of their own.
encryption.how1: Whoever opens the database or a backup sees only gibberish. The master key lies on the server under
encryption.how2: , so that nexdiary itself can read. Whoever has full access to the server therefore gets in; looking in by chance does not work.
encryption.honest: Without the master key a backup cannot be read, not even by you. Older backups also hold the keys of accounts deleted since: with the master key, their diaries in there can still be read.

masterKey.confirmText: With this file and a backup every diary can be read. Keep it apart from the backups. Confirm with your password and your second factor.
masterKey.factorFirst: Set up your own second factor first (My account, Security). Without it nexdiary does not hand out the master key.
masterKey.saved: Master key saved as a file. Keep it apart from the backups.

server.linkSent: The link for {{name}} went to {{email}}. It works once and for 24 hours.
server.linkShown: The link for {{name}}, shown only now, valid once and for 24 hours. Pass it on, the person chooses the password themselves:

ready.title: Ready for the internet?
ready.text: Many reach nexdiary from on the road too. nexdiary checks this itself, every time you open the page.

https.title: Public address with https
https.warn: {{address}} has https, but this request came without. Open nexdiary under that address, or let the proxy send X-Forwarded-Proto.
https.bad: Without https, passwords travel the network in the clear, and Web Push and passkeys do not work at all. Enter the public address with https below.

two_factor.title: Second factor for everybody
two_factor.ok: Whoever signs in with a password needs a code or a passkey as well.
two_factor.bad: Off: a guessed or stolen password is enough to read a diary. Turn on “Require a second factor” below.

own_account.title: Your own account
own_account.bad: Has no second factor yet, and it may change everything. Set it up under My account, Security.

brake.title: Protection against guessing
brake.ok: After 5 wrong tries a 15 minute pause, per account and per address. Every try is in the log.
brake.warn: All visitors come through a proxy nexdiary does not know: the pause holds per account, per address only roughly. See “Behind the proxy”.
brake.bad: The list of trusted proxies holds public networks ({{networks}}). Anybody could then make up the sender's address, and the pause after wrong tries no longer holds. List only the address of your proxy.
brake.broken: The protection against guessing fails its own test. Restart nexdiary; if that does not help, please report it.

encryption.title: Entries encrypted
encryption.ok: Texts, notes, values and photos, each account with a key of its own.
encryption.bad: The master key {{path}} can be read by others too (mode {{mode}}). Set it to 600, the owner only.
encryption.missing: The master key is missing at {{path}}.

cookies.title: Sessions and cookies
cookies.ok: Cookies only over https and not readable by scripts; a sign-in runs out after 30 days without use.
cookies.warn: Without https the sign-in cookies travel in the clear. Over https nexdiary protects them by itself.
cookies.bad: NEXDIARY_COOKIE_SECURE is off: the cookies go unprotected even over https. Set it to auto.

proxy.title: Behind the proxy
proxy.ok: The visitors' real address arrives (proxy {{proxies}} entered as trusted). Without that the protection against guessing would see everybody as one.
proxy.direct: The visitors arrive directly, without a proxy in between.
proxy.warn: The requests come through a proxy ({{proxy}}) that is not entered as trusted: the protection against guessing sees everybody as one. Set NEXDIARY_TRUSTED_PROXIES to its address.
proxy.bad: Public networks are listed as trusted ({{networks}}). Set NEXDIARY_TRUSTED_PROXIES to the address of your proxy, not to the whole internet.

master_key_saved.title: Master key saved
master_key_saved.ok: Last on {{when}}. Keep it apart from the backups.
master_key_saved.warn: Never saved. Without it a backup cannot be read: Server, Backups, Save master key.
